column4: Visit note | 2026-04-06 09:30 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Hafiz Siddique, 23, male. Mr. Siddique presents to the clinic today reporting marks left after pimples as well as active pimples and blackheads on his face. He is a hotel receptionist and mentions that his skin problems have become much worse since starting to work in a hot kitchen in Barishal. He denies any severe systemic symptoms, fever, or pain elsewhere. On examination, he has about 19 inflamed spots on the face. His other vitals are BP 128/77 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, and weight 54 kg. There are no other significant findings. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed; lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage. He was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and do not squeeze spots. Follow-up in 2 months.

Visit note | 2026-04-12 03:00 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Tamanna Uddin, 30, female. Mrs. Uddin attends for a consultation describing a burning sensation behind her breastbone after meals, symptoms that are notably worse when lying down, along with a sour taste in her mouth. She works as a restaurant cook and notes these issues worsened after weeks of eating fried snacks at tea stalls in Narayanganj. She denies dysphagia or unintentional weight loss. On examination, her BMI is 27.8, BP is 136/85 mmHg, pulse is 79 bpm, and weight is 86 kg. Abdominal examination is soft with mild epigastric tenderness. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed; lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage. She was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2026-04-12 04:00 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Rahim Akand, 48, male. Mr. Akand comes in complaining of persistent bloating, symptoms that grow worse with stress, and cramping belly pain. He works as an NGO field officer and explains that his discomfort has escalated since starting a high-pressure job in Cox's Bazar. He has a known history of Hypothyroidism. He denies any bleeding or significant weight changes. On examination, his pain score is 4/10, BP is 118/86 mmHg, pulse is 72 bpm, and weight is 91 kg. His abdomen is soft without tenderness. Assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed; lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage. He was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2026-04-15 11:00 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Saiful Haque, 45, male. Mr. Haque reports experiencing cramping belly pain and bloating. He works as an architect and notes that his symptoms tend to flare up significantly on long commutes through traffic in Jashore. He has a history of Essential hypertension. He denies fever, vomiting, or altered bowel habits of an alarming nature. On examination, his pain score is 5/10, BP is 142/86 mmHg, pulse is 79 bpm, and weight is 51 kg. He was advised to eat regular meals, keep a food diary, and reduce tea, fizzy drinks, and beans. Follow-up in 6 weeks with the food diary.

Visit note | 2026-04-19 04:00 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Nargis Sarkar, 44, female. Mrs. Sarkar attends for a review regarding her chronic sneezing fits, symptoms that are notably worse with dust exposure, and itchy eyes. She works as a mobile phone repair technician and states her condition worsened since keeping a cat at home in Chattogram. She has a history of Hypothyroidism. She denies shortness of breath or skin rashes. On examination, she experiences about 5 sneezing fits a day during consultation. Her other vitals show BP 123/86 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, and weight 58 kg. Nasal mucosa appears mildly congested. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: chronic follow-up: continue current medicines, no new prescription issued, and no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2026-04-21 04:00 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Anika Gazi, 54, female. Mrs. Gazi reports spending all day working indoors and presents with aching bones and frequent muscle cramps. She works as an electrician and noticed these symptoms after working in a windowless office in Bashundhara. She has a documented background of Hypothyroidism. She denies joint swelling or acute trauma. On examination, her vitamin D level is 18 ng/mL, BP is 122/72 mmHg, pulse is 72 bpm, and weight is 82 kg. General physical exam is otherwise unremarkable. Assessment: Vitamin D deficiency. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed; lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage. She was advised to get 20 minutes of morning sunlight daily and eat eggs and fish. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat vitamin D level.

Visit note | 2026-04-26 03:00 PM | Dr. Anisur Rahman, Ophthalmology | Patient: Farhan Rahman, 78, male. Mr. Rahman visits complaining that his symptoms are worse in air conditioning, along with gritty burning eyes and long hours of screen time. He works as a madrasa teacher and notes worsening since night shifts at a call centre in Chattogram. He has a background of Hypothyroidism. He denies double vision or sudden loss of sight. On examination, his tear break-up time is 5 seconds. His other vitals are BP 112/73 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, and weight 55 kg. Corneas appear clear bilaterally. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: referral to Neurology in this clinic for further assessment; no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up after the Neurology review.

Visit note | 2026-04-30 02:30 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Habib Talukder, 60, male. Mr. Talukder comes to the clinic reporting muscle cramps and low energy. He works as a graphic designer and states that his complaints started after staying indoors during a long illness in Sirajganj. He denies any known chronic comorbidities. On examination, his vitamin D level is 18 ng/mL, BP is 121/85 mmHg, pulse is 76 bpm, and weight is 59 kg. Neurological examination of the limbs is normal. Assessment: Vitamin D deficiency. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: serum vitamin D and calcium; no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to get 20 minutes of morning sunlight daily and eat eggs and fish. Follow-up after the test results are ready.
